scope: Theorem 4.1 (Localized linearization) of the manuscript “Lipschitz Equivalent Separable Banach Spaces Need Not Be Linearly Isomorphic” (preprints/Lipschitz-Equivalent-Separable-Banach-Spaces-Need-Not-Be-Linearly-Isomorphic-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 324 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cc670229303a1ed9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (M, ρ, 0) be a complete separable pointed metric space, and let U =   M n≥1 Un   2 be a real Hilbert space with finite-dimensional blocks. Fix an orthonormal basis in every Un, and write Π≥l for projection onto U≥l = ( L n≥l Un)2. Suppose D : M → U is Lipschitz with D(0) = 0, and that for every m ≥ 1 and every distinct z1, . . . , zm ∈ M there are open neighborhoods Oj of zj, an integer l ≥ 1, and mutually orthogonal coordinate subspaces Hj ⊂ U≥l such that Π≥lD(Oj) ⊂ Hj (1 ≤ j ≤ m). (4.1) A coordinate subspace means the closed span of a subset of the fixed orthonormal basis. Then q = b D : F(M) → U is completely continuous.
